newsitem.title: USA: CME to cut 95 staff, slash costs in restructuring.
newsitem.headline: CME to cut 95 staff, slash costs in restructuring.

text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said Wednesday its board approved a sweeping restructuring plan that will cut its 950-person staff by more than 10 percent and slash other spending, resulting in an estimated $17-million-a-year savings.
The board also agreed late Tuesday to waive part of the members' and customers' clearing fees for Aug 1 through Dec 31 this year. The fee waiver will be reviewed annually, a CME spokeswoman said.
The staff reductions are effective immediately, CME said in a press release.
The staff, which held a broad range of positions, were offered severance plans and outplacement services, the exchange said.
CME had 1996 revenues of $164.3 million and operating income of $10.7 million. For first quarter 1997, the exchange said it had revenues of $44 million and operating income of $6.3 million.
It said the restructuring stemmed from "an intensive, strategic review of the budget" as it works to stay competitive in global marketsplaces.
"The board has responded to the will of our membership," said CME chairman emeritus Leo Melamed.

"The global marketplace and our competitive environment are changing every day," said CME chairman Jack Sandner. "In order to continue to lead and innovate, we must position ourselves for the 21st century."
The CME offers futures and futures-options on interest rates, stock indexes, foreign currencies and agricultural commodities.
